title: Bedrock Converse sends tool-result images to models without image support (HTTP 400)
description:
When a tool returns an image on the Bedrock Converse route, `BedrockClient` sends the image as is, even when the model's capabilities say it can't take images. Bedrock then rejects the next request with HTTP 400, so the conversation fails on every later turn.

I can reproduce with a headless Posit Assistant run on `bedrock/us.moonshotai.kimi-k3` (Converse, us-east-1, Windows 11, ai-lib at d4d7a33). In an empty workspace with a 64x64 PNG, I ask "Use your file read tool on pic.png and tell me its dominant color in one word." Step 0 calls the read tool, and step 1 fails:

```
POST /model/us.moonshotai.kimi-k3/converse-stream -> 400 ValidationException
{"message":"This model doesn't support the image field for user messages. Remove image and try again."}
```

In the raw HTTP capture of step 1, the image is inside `toolResult.content`, in the user-role message Converse uses for tool results:

```json
{"toolResult":{"toolUseId":"call_…","content":[{"text":"Image file: pic.png (image/png, 242 bytes, 64×64)"},{"image":{"format":"png","source":{"bytes":"…"}}}]}}
```

There is no separate user image block in the request, so I think the "user messages" in the AWS error refers to that wrapper.

The capabilities look right already. `getBedrockConverseMediaSupport` allows images only for the `anthropic` and `amazon` vendors, so `moonshotai` gets `supportsImages: false` and `supportsToolResultImages: false`:

https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-lib/blob/d4d7a337eca5d07482dd8f3c3ca384410586b367/packages/ai-config/src/model-capabilities/bedrock-defaults.ts#L26-L37

From what I can tell, `BedrockClient` only transforms tool-result images on the Mantle routes (`openai-chat` always, `openai-responses` when `supportsToolResultImages` is falsy). The Converse route never does, so `supportsToolResultImages: false` is ignored there:

https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-lib/blob/d4d7a337eca5d07482dd8f3c3ca384410586b367/packages/ai-provider-bridge/src/model-clients/BedrockClient.ts#L186-L195

`transformToolResultImagesForCompletions` already handles text-only models. With `supportsImages` false it replaces the image with a text note and adds no follow-up user message with an image:

https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-lib/blob/d4d7a337eca5d07482dd8f3c3ca384410586b367/packages/ai-provider-bridge/src/tool-result-images.ts#L158-L161

We could run the same transform on the Converse route when the host passes `supportsToolResultImages: false`. As `supportsToolResultImages` is optional on `ModelClientChatParams`, checking for an explicit `false` there (rather than `!params.supportsToolResultImages` as on Mantle Responses) would keep today's behavior for Claude and Nova when a host doesn't set it. Claude models on the `anthropic-messages` route get `supportsToolResultImages: true` from the same helper, so they would not be affected either.

Things I have not tested:

- Whether Kimi K3 on Bedrock accepts an image in a plain user message. Only the text-only path of the transform is covered by the capabilities above, so it should not matter for this fix.
- Only Kimi K3 was tested. Other non-Anthropic, non-Amazon Converse models get the same capabilities, so I would expect the same 400, but I have not checked.

Possibly related: other clients that never call the transform (DeepSeek, Gemini, Google Vertex, LM Studio, OpenRouter, Snowflake) may hit a similar error with text-only models. Not tested either. #177 is about the same transform, but on the `supportsImages: true` path.

title: Tool-result images moved into a user message trigger AI SDK 7 "image" content part deprecation warning
description:
When a tool result contains an image and the client moves it into a follow-up user message, AI SDK 7 logs a deprecation warning once per process:

```
(node:53268) Warning: AI SDK Warning System: To turn off warning logging, set the AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS global to false.
(node:53268) [AISDK_DEP_IMAGE_CONTENT_PART] DeprecationWarning: AI SDK Warning: Deprecated: ""image" content part". The "image" content part type is deprecated. Use a "file" part with mediaType: 'image' (or a more specific image/* subtype) instead.
```

The request still works and the model sees the image. Only the warning is visible, but in Posit Assistant's terminal UI it prints over the screen, and the user did not attach any image themselves.

I can reproduce with a headless Posit Assistant run on `positai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (`ai` 7.0.147, Windows 11): ask the assistant to read a PNG with its read tool, then send a follow-up turn. Both runs print the warning on stderr, and the follow-up answer shows the model still has the image.

Looking at the logged request, after the tool message there is a user message with the text "Here is the image from the read tool:" followed by the image. That looks like the message built by `transformToolResultImagesForCompletions`, which uses `type: "image"` parts:

https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-lib/blob/d4d7a337eca5d07482dd8f3c3ca384410586b367/packages/ai-provider-bridge/src/tool-result-images.ts#L76-L89

From what I can tell it is called by `PositAiClient`, `OpenAIClient`, `OllamaClient`, `VscodeLmClient`, and `BedrockClient` on the Mantle routes, so all of them would show the same warning when a tool returns an image (a plot, or a read of an image file).

#145 kept `image` parts on purpose, listing the move to the `file` content part as out of scope because it changes what gets written to disk. If I read it right, this message is different: it is rebuilt for each request and never stored. The saved conversation from my repro has the tool result but not this user message. So this one place may not have that concern, but please correct me if I'm missing a path where it gets persisted.

title: Log and show where each provider's credentials come from
description:
When a provider connection fails, the logs usually don't say which credential was used or where it came from. That makes it hard to tell a stale env var from a bad saved key, an expired sign-in, or a missing config file.

#136 fixes this for Google Vertex only: it logs whether the credentials came from the `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` file (and whether that file exists), gcloud's default credentials file, or the metadata server. That came out of posit-dev/positron#16254, where a customer's key file had been deleted and nothing in the logs said so.

Other providers have the same gap. For example:

- If someone has both a saved API key and an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var, we can't tell which one was sent.
- For Bedrock, we can't tell whether credentials came from env vars, an AWS profile (and which one), SSO, or instance metadata.
- In Positron, we can't tell which sign-in session was used.

## Proposal

Have a general way to record where a provider's credentials came from, without logging any secrets, and use it the same way for every provider:

- Log it when credentials are picked up, and include it in auth and network error logs.
- Include it in diagnostic reports.
- Maybe show it in the provider settings UI too, e.g. "Using API key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`".

Vertex can then switch to the shared approach instead of having its own logging.

## Related

#90 asks the same question for config: which layer (enforced, env, user, default, etc.) set a provider's field values. This issue covers credentials. It'd be nice if both answers showed up the same way in logs, diagnostic reports, and the UI.

## Open questions

- How much detail is OK to log? #136 logs file paths, which then end up in diagnostic reports. Env var names and profile names seem fine; values never are.
- Is a settings UI indicator worth doing, or are logs and diagnostic reports enough?

title: Tell consumers which config layer set a field's value, generically
description:
## Background

ai-config's resolver merges several config sources with a fixed order (enforced > legacy-positron-enforced > env > user > legacy-positron > default), but the resolved output doesn't say which layer actually set a given field's value. `ResolvedProvider.connectionProvenance` exists, but it only covers two hardcoded special cases — Bedrock's `aws.region` and Snowflake's `snowflake.connectionName` — each with its own one-off shape. There's no general "which layer set field K on provider P" answer, and right now nothing outside ai-lib itself uses `connectionProvenance`.

This is blocking something concrete in Positron: a `providers.custom` entry with no matching record in the user's `providers.json` could be set by either `default` (should still be user-editable — typing in a new base URL should save) or `enforced` (correctly locked). Positron currently can't tell those two apart, so `extensions/authentication/src/customProviderRegistry.ts`'s save handler treats them the same way (skips the write), which is too strict for the `default` case. Same gap for built-in providers: there's no way for Positron's UI to grey out a field because it's enforced, since nothing tells it that (`positron.d.ts` has no "locked" or "read-only" concept at all).

This came up in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15675.

## Ask

add a general per-field (or at least per-provider) signal to the resolver output — surfaced on `ResolvedProvider` — that says which layer currently owns a given field's value, generalizing what `connectionProvenance` already does instead of adding more special cases per field.

Once this exists, `customProviderRegistry.ts` could treat `default` and `enforced` differently on save, and `connectProviderView.tsx` could grey out a base URL field when it's locked by `enforced`.

title: Provide a way for auth to be handled through custom headers
description:
A user behind an enterprise gateway that authenticates on `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` cannot connect a provider. `customHeaders` excludes five header names (`packages/ai-provider-bridge/src/custom-headers.ts:5-11`), two of which carry credentials: `authorization` and `x-api-key`. Setting either produces no error and no header on the wire.

The exclusion exists because the direct-SDK request path overwrites its own headers with a user's on collision: sending a user header and the built-in credential together would put two conflicting credentials on one request (`memory-bank/architecture.md:239`). Lifting the exclusion for these two names means resolving that conflict instead of leaving it unhandled.

## Proposal

Accept `authorization` and `x-api-key` in `customHeaders`, and suppress the built-in credential for that request when the user supplies either, so exactly one credential goes out.

Leave `accept`, `anthropic-version`, and `content-type` excluded — they carry no credential and overriding them breaks protocol negotiation.

## Design constraints

The exclusion currently lives in the bridge at request time, so a caller that calls `fetch` directly bypasses it. Move the name exclusion into `ai-config`, applied at catalog resolution, so every consumer of a resolved connection gets the same set, and delete the bridge's copy. Keep collision de-duplication per-request, since it needs the request's actual base headers, which don't exist at resolution time. Log when a header is excluded so a surface can tell the user it's never sent rather than silently omitting it.

The editing modal reads the raw user-layer entry byte-for-byte, so an excluded header stays visible and editable in `providers.json` without reaching a request.

For direct-SDK providers, the SDK applies its own headers after the ones it's given, so suppression has to happen when the client is constructed, not when headers merge. The OpenAI-compatible path merges headers itself and can suppress at merge time.

Gemini authenticates with its own API-key header name, which doesn't collide with `authorization`, so validation would send a configured `authorization` header while chat drops it unless filtering happens at resolution rather than only at the direct-SDK/OpenAI-compatible merge points.

## Open questions

Enforced settings merge per key rather than replacing the map (`packages/ai-config/src/enforce.ts:64-85`), so user-supplied keys always survive and an empty enforced map is a no-op. Once a user can override the credential, a Workbench admin has no way to stop them overriding the one their deployment issues. This needs a decision before the change ships.

Whether to warn or fail when a user sets both an auth header and an API key for the same provider, rather than silently preferring one.

## Related

- posit-dev/positron#15248 sends configured headers on validation requests without changing which names are accepted; this issue covers the two names that fix leaves out.
- posit-dev/assistant-feedback#46 requests the same capability.
- posit-dev/assistant#1066 added header support on the chat path.

title: Generalize apiKeyOptional across custom provider kinds
description:
## Context

#109 added `apiKeyOptional: true` for **custom Anthropic** entries only. The anthropic-only scoping was deliberate — it's the only additional kind with wire-level anonymous support — but it introduces per-kind special cases that would disappear if the option were general:

- `schema.ts`: the field is bolted onto the anthropic variant via `.extend()` instead of living in the shared `customProviderVariantSchema` factory; fragments may carry it for any kind but only anthropic survives merged validation.
- `resolve-catalog.ts`: `resolveAuthPolicies` needs the `entry.type === "anthropic" ? entry.apiKeyOptional : undefined` conditional.

Generalizing would remove those, but most of #109's bulk is scoping-independent and stays: `ResolvedCustomAuthPolicy` + provenance resolution, the `CUSTOM_KIND_API_KEY_OPTIONAL_DEFAULT` mirror + shape guard, the watcher classification, and the wire-level client handling.

## What generalizing requires

The per-kind work relocates rather than vanishes: each newly-supported kind needs its own anonymous-mode wire handling (the Anthropic sentinel/header-strip exists because the SDK falls back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; the OpenAI SDK has the same `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback problem), plus wire-level tests proving no auth header or ambient env var leaks. Kinds already key-optional by default (`openai-compatible`, `litellm`, `portkey`) would treat the field as redundant-but-harmless.

## Why do it

- Removes the schema/resolution special cases above (small win, ~20-30 lines plus comments).
- Avoids a schema migration later if more kinds gain anonymous support.
- Natural stepping stone toward posit-dev/assistant-feedback#102, which asks for `apiKeyOptional` on **built-in** providers (built-in `anthropic`/`openai`/`gemini` pointed at a pre-authenticated corporate gateway). The layered-config provenance machinery from #109 already generalizes; the remaining work is per-protocol wire behavior and UI surfaces accepting a blank key.

Not urgent — file for future consideration.

title: Custom provider: support Anthropic Messages API for Claude models
description:
Split from https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/13817, to capture the Umbrella Provider support separately.

For Umbrella Providers, some providers may offer both Anthropic and OpenAI models, but expect requests to the Anthropic models to use the messages API.

This is more possible now that we have the providers.json spec. We probably want to somehow detect on the user's behalf which api type should be used for the endpoint, possibly based on model name. This would likely be done at the ai-lib provider bridge level.

---

Some gateways serve both OpenAI and Claude models, and want Claude requests sent Anthropic-style (`/messages`) and everything else OpenAI-style.
We already handle this for LiteLLM, Portkey and OpenCode, but a generic `openai-compatible` custom provider sends every model OpenAI-style.
Users can set `models.overrides["<id>"].protocol`, but the openai-compatible provider only accepts `openai-chat` and `openai-responses`, and `anthropic-messages` throws `Unsupported protocol for OpenAI`.

Approach: expand the existing `openai-compatible` type rather than adding a new provider type.

## Work Items

- [ ] Let openai-compatible accept `protocol: "anthropic-messages"` per model
- [ ] Route those models to an Anthropic client on the same gateway (like the LiteLLM provider)
- [ ] Use Anthropic capabilities for those models (prompt caching, thinking)
- [ ] Document the override in the providers.json docs
- [ ] Follow-up (optional): guess the protocol from the model name, behind a provider-level switch

## Notes

- Example config:

  ```json
  "custom": {
    "My Gateway": {
      "type": "openai-compatible",
      "baseUrl": "https://ai.mycompany.com/v1",
      "models": { "overrides": { "claude-sonnet-4-5": { "protocol": "anthropic-messages" } } }
    }
  }
  ```

- No schema change expected, since `protocol` on overrides already exists.
- Auto-detection needs to be optional, since some gateways only speak OpenAI format, even for Claude.
- Open question: how to handle auth on the Anthropic route (Bearer vs `x-api-key`), since gateways differ.
- Once this ships, bump the ai-lib pin in assistant.

title: Claude Fable 5 on Bedrock returns raw 400 (data retention mode 'default' not available)
description:
### Summary

Selecting **Claude Fable 5** on the Amazon Bedrock provider and sending any message returns HTTP 400 before generation:

```
data retention mode 'default' is not available for this model
```

Claude Fable 5 (and Claude Mythos 5) require 30-day data retention per Anthropic policy and cannot run under zero/"default" data retention. On Bedrock this requirement is enforced by the platform. We surface the raw 400 rather than handling it.

### Environment (reproduced)

- Posit Assistant 0.8.0, Positron 2026.08.0 (build 124), Darwin arm64
- Provider: Amazon Bedrock
- Model: `claude-fable-5` (very likely `claude-mythos-5` too — same 30-day retention requirement)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Bedrock provider and select Claude Fable 5.
2. Send any message.
3. Request fails with HTTP 400: `data retention mode 'default' is not available for this model`.

### Notes / background

- This is **not** the `eager_input_streaming` issue (#33 / PR #34) — different root cause and fix location, filed separately.
- We already know Fable 5 / Mythos 5 are the 30-day-retention exception: see the model descriptions in `packages/core/src/utils/model-helpers.ts` (~L294–299), which note that, unlike other Posit AI models (zero data retention), Fable 5 / Mythos 5 retain data for 30 days.
- Our Bedrock path (`packages/ai-provider-bridge/src/model-clients/BedrockClient.ts`) does not set any data-retention parameter on the request, so the "default" mode is coming from the account/SDK default.

### Root cause not yet confirmed

Unclear whether this is:

1. **AWS Bedrock account / inference-profile configuration** — the account's data-retention mode doesn't meet Fable 5's 30-day requirement (would be resolved on the AWS side, not in our code), or
2. **Something the client should send or handle** — e.g. a retention-mode parameter, or model availability that we should detect.

### Suggested directions

- Confirm whether configuring appropriate data retention on the Bedrock account resolves it (rules in/out the account-config hypothesis).
- If it's account config: document the requirement, and consider surfacing a clear, actionable message instead of the raw 400, and/or gating/annotating Fable 5 + Mythos 5 on the Bedrock provider.
- If it's a request parameter: determine whether/how to pass a data-retention mode on the Bedrock request for these models.

### Also affects

Likely `claude-mythos-5` on Bedrock (same retention requirement) — worth confirming during investigation.

title: ai-config: concurrent rebuilds in watchResolvedProviderCatalog drop or invert change events
providers.json writes fail with EPERM on Windows when anything else has the file open
description:
**In plain English:** say you're on Windows with Positron open in two windows. You connect an AI provider for the first time -- paste your API key, click Connect. Instead of connecting, you get a raw error like:

```
EPERM: operation not permitted, rename
'C:\Users\you\.posit\ai\providers.json.tmp.9028'
-> 'C:\Users\you\.posit\ai\providers.json'
```

Nothing is wrong with your key. What happened is that the *other* window was reading the shared provider-settings file at the moment this window tried to replace it. On Windows, replacing a file that another process has open fails outright rather than waiting; on macOS and Linux the same operation just succeeds, which is why this is Windows-only. Clicking Connect again usually works, because the other reader has finished by then.

It's timing-dependent, so an individual user won't hit it often. But our Windows e2e lane -- which runs three Positron instances against one settings file -- hits it about 10% of the time, which is what surfaced this.

---

### Where it is

`packages/ai-config/src/node/mutate-config.ts`, `atomicWrite` (~L185). It writes a temp file and then renames it over the target with a **single, unretried** `fs.rename`:

```ts
const tempPath = `${configPath}.tmp.${process.pid}`;
await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
try {
    await fs.writeFile(tempPath, text, { encoding: "utf-8", mode: 0o644 });
    await fs.rename(tempPath, configPath);   // <-- EPERM here on Windows
} finally {
    try { await fs.unlink(tempPath); } catch { /* already renamed */ }
}
```

`mutateProvidersConfig` does hold a `proper-lockfile` lock, so it serializes **writers**. It does nothing about **readers**, and readers are what break the rename.

The competing reads are largely self-inflicted, so this reproduces even in a single process:

- Positron's `extensions/authentication/src/providerCatalog.ts` calls `refreshProviderCatalog()` immediately after every mutation, which re-reads the file.
- `ai-config`'s own watcher (`watch-catalog.ts` L175) watches the parent directory and fires on `providers.json`, scheduling a 300ms-debounced re-read after every successful write.

So each write schedules reads that can land on top of the next write's rename.

### Same pattern in ai-credentials

`packages/ai-credentials/src/store/SingleFileStore.ts`, `writeStore()` (~L318) has an identical unretried temp-file + `fs.rename`. That file holds the user's actual credentials, so the same contention can silently fail to save an API key. Worth fixing in the same pass, ideally via one shared helper.

### Mechanism confirmed empirically

Windows 11, Node v24, against a scratch file:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| baseline, no open handles | rename **succeeded** |
| open read handle on the **destination** | rename **failed, EPERM** |
| open read handle on the **source** temp file | rename **succeeded** |
| after the handle was released | rename **succeeded** |

Conclusions: an ordinary reader holding `providers.json` open is sufficient; "antivirus scanning the freshly written temp file" is **ruled out** as the mechanism; and a retry is a **validated** fix.

### Scope of the failure

The connect aborts cleanly -- it does **not** leave half-saved state. In Positron's `handleApiKeySave` (`extensions/authentication/src/configDialog.ts`), the config write (`onSave`) runs *before* `provider.storeKey(...)`, so an EPERM there aborts the whole operation and no credential is stored. The user-visible cost is a failed connect showing a raw Node error, recoverable by retrying.

Note the write only happens when the mutation actually changes bytes (see gotcha 1 below), so in practice this bites **first-time** provider setup rather than reconnecting an already-configured provider.

### Reproducing it

Hold a read handle open on `~/.posit/ai/providers.json` while a connect runs:

```js
const fs = require('fs');
const fd = fs.openSync(process.env.HOME + '/.posit/ai/providers.json', 'r');
// ... run the connect ... then:
fs.closeSync(fd);
```

Two gotchas that make a naive repro silently useless:

1. `mutate-config.ts` short-circuits **before** `atomicWrite`: `if (output === raw) { return; }`. If `providers.json` already contains the provider block the connect would write, there is no write, no rename, and no EPERM -- the attempt just succeeds and looks like it disproves the bug. Delete the provider's block first.
2. The temp file is `providers.json.tmp.${process.pid}`, so **every retry inside one process reuses the same filename**. Watching the directory for new temp filenames yields exactly one sighting no matter how many attempts occur -- don't build trigger logic on distinct temp names.

### Proposed fix

Retry the rename with bounded backoff on the Windows-transient errnos (`EPERM`, `EACCES`, `EBUSY`; consider `ENOTEMPTY`) -- roughly 5-10 attempts over a few hundred ms.

- Keep the total budget well under `mutate-config.ts`'s 10s `stale` lock timeout, so a retrying writer can never outlive its own lock.
- Only retry those errnos; a genuine permanent permission error must still surface.
- Prefer one shared helper used by both `ai-config` and `ai-credentials` over two copies.
- Leave POSIX behaviour unchanged -- the first rename succeeds there, so the retry path is never entered. An errno check is enough; no need to gate on `process.platform` (and an errno check also covers network/container filesystems).
- On final failure, throw an error naming the file and stating the write did not land, so callers can surface something better than a raw `EPERM` string.
- Keep the `finally { unlink(tempPath) }` cleanup correct across the retry loop.

Consider additionally performing the post-write reads under the same lock, which would remove the self-inflicted collision rather than just tolerating it.

### Tests

`ai-config` uses Vitest (`packages/ai-config/src/__tests__/`); extend the existing `mutate-config.test.ts`. Suggested cases:

- rename fails `EPERM` twice then succeeds -> write lands, no error, temp file gone
- rename fails for the whole budget -> throws, error names the path, temp file cleaned up
- a non-transient error (e.g. `EROFS`) -> throws immediately, **no** retries
- success on first attempt -> exactly one rename call (guards the POSIX no-op claim)

Inject the failure rather than stubbing globals: take an optional rename-like dependency defaulting to the real implementation, consistent with how the surrounding tests already fake the filesystem. Add equivalent coverage for `SingleFileStore.writeStore()`.

### Onset / context

Positron's Windows e2e test `Posit Assistant Sign-in > anthropic-api - Sign in, send hello, sign out` started failing 2026-08-25, win/electron only (~10%; every other platform 100% green). Example run: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/33418599892

`atomicWrite` has not changed since 2026-08-10 (`48988a4`), so the onset correlates with Positron's ai-lib bump rather than a change to this function -- correlation, not a proven cause. Still present in `a05f21e9`, the submodule Positron main currently points at.

A temporary retry stopgap lives in Positron's e2e page object (posit-dev/positron#15830) so CI isn't blocked; it should be removed when this is fixed.

title: ai-credentials exports are ESM-only, blocking CommonJS consumers like Positron's extensions/authentication
description:
## Problem

`extensions/authentication` in Positron can't import from `ai-credentials`, even though it wants `CUSTOM_CLIENT_KIND_AUTH_MAP` from `ai-credentials/types` instead of keeping its own local copy.

## Why

`extensions/authentication` compiles to CommonJS (no `"type": "module"`, `module: nodenext`). Node resolves a package's CommonJS `require()` calls using the `require` condition in that package's `exports` map. `ai-credentials/package.json` only defines `types` and `import` conditions, no `require`, so it's ESM-only and can't be loaded from a CommonJS consumer.

For comparison, `ai-config` (which Positron already depends on) defines both `import` and `require` for its exports, which is why that one works fine as a dependency here.

## Ask

Add a `require` condition to `ai-credentials`'s `package.json` exports map, matching the pattern already used by `ai-config`, so CommonJS consumers like Positron's `extensions/authentication` can depend on it directly instead of duplicating its types/constants locally.

## Note for whoever picks this up

Double-check there isn't a deliberate reason `ai-credentials` was kept import-only (e.g. it pulls in something without a safe CJS story) before just copying the `ai-config` exports shape over.

## Reference

posit-dev/positron#15675

title: Assistant: Support defaultThinkingEffort in custom model definitions (providers.json)
description:
## Problem Description:

When configuring custom language models in `~/.posit/ai/providers.json`, users can declare available thinking levels via `thinkingEffortLevels`, for example:
```json
"thinkingEffortLevels": [
  "low",
  "medium",
  "high",
  "max"
]
```

However, there is currently no way to declare a **default** thinking effort for a model (e.g. `"defaultThinkingEffort": "high"`).

### Impact:

1. **Initial conversation state defaults to null**: When a new conversation begins, the session state initializes `thinkingEffort: null`.
2. **Missing reasoning payload**: Unless the user manually clicks the thinking effort selector in the UI for every new conversation, the outgoing request to the model provider omits the `reasoning` parameter entirely (`reasoningEffort` is not included in the payload).
3. **Suboptimal performance for reasoning models**: Controllable reasoning models (such as o-series, GPT-5/6, Gemini 2.5/3.x, Qwen, etc.) fall back to zero or minimal reasoning effort by default, defeating the purpose of configuring a reasoning model.

### Proposed Solution:

Add support for an optional `defaultThinkingEffort` property in model definitions within `providers.json`:
```json
{
  "id": "my-provider/my-reasoning-model",
  "name": "My Reasoning Model",
  "protocol": "openai-responses",
  "thinkingEffortLevels": ["low", "medium", "high", "max"],
  "defaultThinkingEffort": "high"
}
```

When a conversation selects this model, Positron Assistant should automatically initialize the conversation's `thinkingEffort` with the declared `defaultThinkingEffort` instead of `null`.

title: Per-protocol capability profiles: overriding a model's protocol should re-derive inferred capabilities
description:
Follow-up to #61 (Databricks native APIs), which documents this limitation in `memory-bank/aiConfig.md`.

## Problem

Protocol-stamping providers (LiteLLM, and now Databricks) infer a model's capabilities *for the protocol they stamp*. A natively-routed Databricks Claude model advertises `thinkingEffortLevels` and PDF input because the `anthropic-messages` route supports them; the same endpoint forced onto `openai-chat` (via a user protocol override or a connection-level `protocol`) does not support those capabilities — but it keeps the stamped ones.

The generic fix ("mask capabilities when final protocol ≠ stamp") was considered and withdrawn during planning: `resolveModels` merges user capability overrides into the flat model object *before* `attachRouting`, so a pipeline mask cannot distinguish user-supplied capability values from inferred ones, and no safe protocol-keyed mask exists post-merge.

## Proposed direction

Introduce a provenance/profile seam in the resolution pipeline: carry inferred capabilities as a per-protocol profile (or tag capability values with their provenance — inferred vs user override) so that when the final resolved protocol differs from the discovery stamp, inferred capabilities can be re-derived for the actual route while user overrides still win.

## Scope notes

- Pre-existing limitation for LiteLLM; Databricks native routing widens the surface.
- Related: a profile-key transport through chat params (separate issue) could share the same seam.

title: Native Gemini routing for arbitrarily-named external endpoints: carry a profile key through chat params
description:
Follow-up to #61 (Databricks native APIs), which defers this.

## Problem

Databricks native Gemini routing (`google-generative` protocol stamp) is restricted to endpoints whose *name* positively identifies the thinking variant (hosted pay-per-token names like `databricks-gemini-2-5-pro`). This is because `ModelClientChatParams` carries only `model` + `thinkingEffort` — at chat time, `GeminiGenerateContentClient` must re-derive the variant profile (budget vs level thinking control, ranges, off-ability) from the model string via ai-config's `getGeminiGenerateContentProfile`.

An external Gemini endpoint named e.g. `my-gemini-endpoint` backed by `gemini-2.5-flash` is classified correctly at discovery (the classifier sees `external_model.name`), but the client would have no way to reconstruct the variant from the endpoint name, so discovery deliberately stamps `openai-chat` instead (the classifier and client share one helper so stamp and wire choice cannot disagree).

## Proposed direction

Widen the chat-params seam so the catalog pipeline can carry a discovery-time profile key (e.g. the resolved underlying model identity or a variant/profile id) into `ModelClientChatParams`. The client would prefer the carried key and fall back to name-derivation. Cross-repo change: bridge type plus catalog pipeline plumbing in consumers.

## Scope notes

- Only worth doing if external Gemini endpoints on Databricks (or similar gateways) matter to users; hosted pay-per-token Gemini already routes natively.
- Could share the seam proposed in #62 (per-protocol capability provenance).

title: ai-config: add character and case rules to customProviderNameIssues
ai-config: add a displayName field to custom provider entries
description:
Positron is adding UI for multiple named custom providers (posit-dev/positron#12747), where the user types a name at creation time. That name becomes the `providers.custom` key, and the key is also the provider id, so the name can't be changed afterwards without re-keying everything filed under it.

`build-catalog.ts` mints the id straight from the entry key, and there's no separate label:

```ts
for (const [name, entry] of Object.entries(customEntries)) {
    const customId = mintCustomProviderId(name);
    ...
    catalog.push({ id: customId, clientKind: entry.type, ... });
}
```

`customProviderVariantSchema` is `.strict()`, so a user can't hand-author a display label either.

What that costs today, in both products:

- Renaming means rewriting the `providers.custom` key, re-keying the credential record, re-registering the auth provider, and rewriting any persisted default-model selection that names the provider. Every one of those can half-succeed.
- Posit Assistant deferred rename in posit-dev/assistant#2056 for exactly this reason: "Rename requires coordinated provider-ID, credential, and default-model/settings migration; v1 remains delete and re-add."
- Positron has the same request open as posit-dev/positron#14141, unscheduled. Naming-at-creation covers the complaint that prompted it, so without this field the answer there is also delete and re-add, and that's an acceptable answer rather than a blocked one.
- An admin shipping a `providers.custom` entry through a default or enforced layer has to encode the label in the key, so the key has to double as human-facing copy.

With a separate `displayName`, rename becomes cosmetic: the key stays put, credentials and model selections never move, and the UI is a plain text field with no migration behind it.

### Proposed change in `ai-config`

- Add `displayName: z.string().min(1).optional()` to `customProviderVariantSchema`, as a sibling of `type` rather than a connection field, and to `customProviderEntryFragmentSchema` so a fragment can set it alone. Regenerate `providers.schema.json` through `scripts/generate-schema.ts`.
- Add `readonly displayName: string | undefined` to `ResolvedProvider`, and set it in the custom-provider loop in `build-catalog.ts`. `mintCustomProviderId(name)` keeps minting the id from the key, so ids and credentials are untouched.
- Resolve it through the existing layer precedence like any other entry field, so a default layer can suggest a label and an enforced layer can pin one.

Consumers then render `displayName ?? id`, and nothing changes when the field is absent.

### Not asking for

- Id rename or any migration machinery. The point of the field is to make that unnecessary.
- `displayName` on built-in provider blocks. Both products hard-code those names.
- Uniqueness validation. The entry key stays the identity; two entries sharing a label is a UI concern, not a schema one.

Related: posit-dev/positron#14141, which is unscheduled. Nothing in Positron is waiting on this, so treat it as a schema improvement to take or leave on its own merits rather than a blocker.

title: Databricks chat fails when a model sends reasoning content blocks
description:
## Problem

Chat with a Databricks model fails when the model sends reasoning.

The Databricks Unity AI Gateway sends reasoning as an array of content blocks in `choices[].delta.content`. The OpenAI chat completions format defines `content` as a string. The chunk schema in `@ai-sdk/openai` enforces the string type. One array chunk fails the schema check, and then the stream stops.

Model discovery uses a different API, so the provider lists all models correctly. Only chat fails. As a result, the problem looks like an authentication fault. A personal access token and an OAuth token both fail. Authentication is not the cause.

## Error

The Posit Assistant output panel shows this error:

```
Type validation failed: Value: {"model":"us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5","choices":[{"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"reasoning","summary":[{"type":"summary_text","text":"","signature":"EqIM..."}]}]},"index":0,"finish_reason":null}], ...}
Error message: [
  {
    "expected": "string",
    "code": "invalid_type",
    "path": ["choices", 0, "delta", "content"],
    "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received array"
  }
]
```

## Models

Only the models that send reasoning fail.

| Model | `delta.content` | Chat |
|---|---|---|
| `databricks-gpt-oss-120b` | array | fails |
| `databricks-claude-sonnet-5` | array | fails |
| `databricks-claude-opus-5` | array | fails |
| `databricks-claude-haiku-4-5` | string | works |
| `databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct` | string | works |

## How to see the problem

1. Configure the Databricks provider with a workspace URL and a token.
2. Select the model `databricks-gpt-oss-120b`.
3. Send this prompt: `What is 2+2? Think step by step, then answer.`
4. Read the Posit Assistant output panel. The panel shows `Type validation failed`.

Note: `databricks-claude-sonnet-5` sends reasoning for some prompts only. Use `databricks-gpt-oss-120b` for a reliable result.

You can also see the wire format with one command:

```bash
curl -sN -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  "$HOST/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions" \
  -d '{"model":"databricks-gpt-oss-120b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 2+2? Think briefly."}],"stream":true}'
```

Some chunks hold a string. Other chunks hold an array:

```json
{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":[{"type":"reasoning","summary":[{"type":"summary_text","text":"The user asks simple"}]}]},"index":0}]}
```

## Cause

This is not a regression. Three facts show this:

- The chunk schema is the same in `@ai-sdk/openai` 3.0.72 and 3.0.88. Version 3.0.72 was the version when the provider merged.
- Two commits changed `databricks-provider.ts`. The second commit changed the constructor signature only.
- Claude 4.x models and Llama models send a string. These models were the test models for the first release.

The gap was in the code from the start. Databricks then added models that send reasoning, and the gap became visible.

## Scope

A non-streaming response holds the same blocks at `choices[].message.content`. The assistant always streams, so this path is unreachable today.

title: Add an Enforced Host layer in the configuration resolution precedence order
description:
https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-lib/blame/6745f4f233f6cefd711b75c0f0f85c64253ee6d2/packages/ai-config/src/resolve-catalog.ts#L42-L46 lists out the precedence order of various configuration sources:
 1. `enforced` — sealed admin overlay (`POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED`); always wins.
 1. `user` — the user's `providers.json`.
 1. `host` — transitional host settings (Positron `authentication.*`).
 1.  `default` — Workbench admin defaults (`POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_DEFAULT`).

This issue proposes adding a 5th option, `enforced host` (or `enforcedHost`), which will
1. take precedence after `enforced`, but before `user`
2. read and apply the settings from the `POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS` environment variable, which is a JSON blob that (optionally) contains some of Positron's `settings.json`

title: Bedrock/Snowflake eager_input_streaming 400 occurring for several models
description:
### Summary

Streaming a tool-use request to **Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Amazon Bedrock** fails with HTTP 400 before any generation happens:

```
tools.0.custom.eager_input_streaming: Extra inputs are not permitted
```

`@ai-sdk/anthropic` adds `eager_input_streaming: true` to tool specs by default while streaming. Some Anthropic models on Bedrock reject that field. `BedrockClient` already opts out of it (via `toolStreaming: false`), but the opt-out is scoped to Haiku 4.5 only, so Sonnet 4.5 still sends the field and gets rejected.

### Environment (reproduced)

**Posit Assistant**
- Version: 0.8.0
- Platform: Positron
- Positron: 2026.08.0 (build 124)
- OS: Darwin 25.5.0, arm64
- Runtime: Node.js v24.15.0
- Build: release, Git Commit: e36aec6, Build Date: Jul 17, 2026

- Provider: Amazon Bedrock
- Model: Claude Sonnet 4.5 (`anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-*` / `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-*`)
- Path: `createBedrockAnthropic` (native Anthropic InvokeModel through Bedrock)

### Root cause

In `packages/ai-provider-bridge/src/model-clients/BedrockClient.ts`, the opt-out is gated on the model ID containing `claude-haiku-4-5`:

```ts
// Haiku 4.5 on Bedrock rejects the `eager_input_streaming` field that
// @ai-sdk/anthropic adds to tools by default while streaming, returning HTTP 400.
// Other Anthropic models on Bedrock accept it, so scope the opt-out to Haiku 4.5;
const disableEagerToolStreaming = params.model.includes("claude-haiku-4-5");
```

A Sonnet 4.5 Bedrock model ID does not contain `claude-haiku-4-5`, so `toolStreaming: false` is never set, the AI SDK sends `eager_input_streaming`, and this Bedrock model rejects it. The inline comment's assumption that "other Anthropic models on Bedrock accept it" is too narrow.

`SnowflakeClient.ts` carries the identical Haiku-only guard (its comment says "matching the Bedrock fix") and has the same latent bug.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Bedrock provider with Claude Sonnet 4.5.
2. Send a message that lets the model call a tool (tool streaming is on by default).
3. Request fails with HTTP 400: `tools.0.custom.eager_input_streaming: Extra inputs are not permitted`.

### Expected

Tool-use streaming works on Sonnet 4.5 on Bedrock, same as on the direct Anthropic provider.

### Suggested fix

The accept/reject matrix is a Bedrock-side quirk that has already drifted once (Haiku 4.5, now Sonnet 4.5). Rather than maintain a per-model allow/deny list, disable eager tool streaming for **all** Anthropic models on Bedrock (and Snowflake). It is a latency optimization, not a correctness feature, so turning it off is safe:

```ts
const disableEagerToolStreaming = isAnthropic;
```

Alternatively, keep the per-model guard and add `claude-sonnet-4-5`. Either way, add a regression test asserting `toolStreaming: false` is passed for the affected models. There is currently no test coverage for this opt-out.

### Notes

- Related to https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-provider-bridge/pull/14, https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-provider-bridge/pull/18 (similar previous fixes).
- Repo was `posit-dev/ai-provider-bridge`, now `posit-dev/ai-lib`; the old name in the code comment redirects.

title: Add missing connection env mappings and AWS profile shaping
description:
Positron is migrating core and the `authentication` extension's credential-chain reads onto the resolved catalog (posit-dev/positron#14710). Those consumers read a few env vars directly today; the catalog needs to fold them, and credential shaping lacks one field.

`CONNECTION_ENV_MAPPINGS` gaps (`ConnectionEnvMapping` has no `snowflake` field yet):

- `snowflake-cortex`: `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT` -> `snowflake.account`, `SNOWFLAKE_HOME` -> `snowflake.home`.
- `google-vertex`: `GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL` -> `baseUrl`; legacy `GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT` / `GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION` as fallbacks when `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` / `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` are unset.

Credential shaping: `CredentialConfig` has no AWS profile getter, so a catalog-configured `aws.profile` never reaches the shaped credential. Add `getAwsProfile()` and set `profile` in the `aws-credentials` output.

Blocker of posit-dev/positron#14710

title: Enforced connection fields can be overridden by a user's environment variables
description:
# Enforced connection fields can be overridden by a user's environment variables

## Summary

The `POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED` overlay is meant to be non-overridable. That holds for enablement and for connection fields set through config files, but not for the connection fields that have an environment-variable mapping. A user who sets an ordinary environment variable in their own shell (`POSITAI_AUTH_HOST`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `AWS_REGION`, and the others in `CONNECTION_ENV_MAPPINGS`) overrides the enforced value for that field.

Admins set the `ENFORCED` overlay precisely to lock these fields, so a per-user workaround defeats the control's purpose.

## Root cause

Connection config and enablement resolve on two different paths.

Enablement folds every source, enforced first, in `resolveEnabled` ("first defined wins," enforced on top) — sound.

Connection config takes a longer path in `buildCatalog`:

```
resolveConnection(id, block)        // merges sources; enforced wins here
  -> applyEnvOverlay(id, ..., envVars)   // runs AFTER, unconditionally
```

`applyEnvOverlay` (`build-catalog.ts:289`) applies the environment overlay after the enforced merge, and its own contract states "Env vars have the highest precedence: env > file (providers.json) > defaults" (`build-catalog.ts:285`). The `envVars` it reads is plain `process.env`, injected by the node seam (`load-catalog.ts:42`), the same object for every user. The mapped variables in `CONNECTION_ENV_MAPPINGS` (`build-catalog.ts:51`) are ordinary environment variables, not the sealed `POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED` fragment. Nothing between `process.env` and the overlay distinguishes an admin-set variable from a user-set one.

The layering is inverted: the environment overlay represents user/host intent but is applied above the admin's enforced layer.

The existing test "enforced connection can never be overridden by lower sources" (`__tests__/resolve-catalog.test.ts:74`) only exercises file and `default` sources with `envVars: {}`, so it never covers the environment path where the invariant fails.

title: Expose model capability inference for reuse outside the bridge
ai-config: add a `snowflake.home` field to the providers.json schema
description:
Positron is migrating its AI provider settings to providers.json. One of the settings, `authentication.snowflake.credentials.SNOWFLAKE_HOME`, has no destination in the schema: the `snowflake` connection section carries only `account` and `host`.

`SNOWFLAKE_HOME` points credential detection at a non-default directory containing `connections.toml`. In Positron it is read by the authentication extension's Snowflake credential discovery, with the `SNOWFLAKE_HOME` env var as fallback. It is important for Snowflake Managed Credentials in Workbench, which place `connections.toml` in a managed location that credential detection must be pointed at.

Proposed change in `ai-config`:

- Add `home` to `snowflakeConfigSchema` (`account`, `host`, `home`) and regenerate `providers.schema.json`.
- Carry it through `ResolvedConnection.snowflake` and the `snowflake` merge in `build-catalog.ts`.
- Extend the `ai-config/positron` snowflake read (`PositronAuthSettingReader.getSnowflake` and the `"snowflake"` descriptor) so the transitional host layer picks it up from `authentication.snowflake.credentials.SNOWFLAKE_HOME`.

Blocks posit-dev/positron#14708.

title: ai-config emits extensionless relative imports that break nodenext consumers
description:
ai-config builds with `moduleResolution: "bundler"` and emits extensionless relative specifiers into `dist/` (`export * from "../index"`, `from "./vocabulary"`). Bundlers resolve these, but Node ESM and TypeScript's `nodenext` resolution require explicit extensions.

Positron hit both failure modes while wiring the providers.json settings migration (posit-dev/positron#14708). The consuming `authentication` extension runs in the Node extension host, so its TypeScript resolves modules with `nodenext` and its extension-host tests execute plain tsc output under Node ESM semantics:

- Type checking cannot follow the `export * from "../index"` chain in `dist/node/index.d.ts`, so every re-exported type is invisible: `extensions/authentication/src/migration/providersJson.ts(6,15): error TS2305: Module '"ai-config/node"' has no exported member 'ProvidersConfig'.`
- At runtime, `await import('ai-config/node')` loads `dist/node/index.js` with real Node ESM semantics and fails on the first extensionless relative import.

Fix: add `.js` extensions to relative import/export specifiers in ai-config's source and switch its tsconfig to `module`/`moduleResolution` `nodenext` so a regression fails the build. Both are compatible with the existing esbuild consumers.

title: An interrupted first write leaves providers.json empty, and Posit Assistant stays broken
description:
## Problem

`~/.posit/ai/providers.json` can be left empty, and from then on Posit Assistant stays broken until someone deletes the file:

- Every load reports `Failed to load .../providers.json: Invalid JSONC: ValueExpected at line 1, column 1. Using empty config.`, which Posit Assistant shows as an error toast.
- Every mutation fails with `[ai-config] Cannot mutate .../providers.json: ValueExpected at line 1, column 1. Mutation aborted until the file is fixed.` For example, Positron cannot apply Workbench's Posit AI Pass default.
- `readUserCustomProviderEntries` throws as well.

## Cause

The first mutation creates the file in two steps: `raceSafeEnsureFile` in `packages/ai-config/src/node/mutate-config.ts` opens it with the exclusive `wx` flag, which leaves it empty, and then writes the `$schema` and `version` seed through that descriptor. Later mutations go through `atomicWrite`, but this first step is not atomic.

If the process stops between the two steps, the file stays empty. A watcher on the file saw it go from absent to 0 bytes, then to 159 bytes 35 ms later. A window reload during that gap, which stops the extension host, left it at 0 bytes for good.

Nothing reseeds it:

- The next mutation's `wx` open sees `EEXIST`.
- `readCurrentConfig` then refuses the empty content as invalid JSONC.

We hit this in automated Workbench tests that open a folder a few seconds after Positron starts. A user reloading the window, or an extension host restarting, during first start-up would hit the same thing.

## Fix

An empty or whitespace-only file holds no configuration, so treat it as missing:

- Loading reports no issue.
- Reading custom provider entries returns an empty map.
- The next mutation seeds the file as if it had created it.

That makes the interrupted creation harmless, and repairs files that are already empty.

title: Build one self-contained headless bundle in ai-lib for Positron and Posit Assistant
description:
Positron and Posit Assistant are going to each bundle the `ai-provider-bridge/headless` entry with esbuild. Each repo has its own esbuild config for this, and the two configs are different. Should we consider making one self-contained bundle in ai-lib, and use it in both places?

### Background

Positron's server loads `ai-provider-bridge/headless` for the headless language model features, such as the suggestions in the notebook Assistant panel. Before posit-dev/positron#17276, the server build copied the entry and its 119 dependency packages into `node_modules`. That was about 5,500 files (about 1,850 after a separate prune). posit-dev/positron#17276 is setting this up so we bundle the entry with esbuild in Positron's build and the server will now ships 13 files. (We're working on reducing file counts because it's a problem for Workbench startup times with NFS.)

Posit Assistant already builds its own bundle of the same entry, `dist/provider-module/index.js`, in `packages/positron/esbuild.ts`. Positron loads this copy in place of its own when the installed Assistant is newer than the Assistant that ships with Positron, and when the headless contract version matches.

The same entry gets bundled two times, by two configs, from two ai-lib commits.

### How the two bundles are different

| | Positron (`build/lib/ai-lib-server-bundle.ts`) | Assistant (`packages/positron/esbuild.ts`) |
|---|---|---|
| Output | `headless.js` and 10 lazy chunks | One file |
| Module resolution | Default `mainFields`, `conditions: []`, and a plugin that points `jsonc-parser` at its ESM build | `mainFields: ["module", "main"]` |
| Builds that the bundle contains | The same builds that Node loads (CommonJS for the AWS SDK) | The `module` builds (`dist-es` for the AWS SDK) |
| Minified | No | Yes, in production |
| License notices | `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` from the esbuild metafile | Not in the bundle output |
| Checks on the output | File budget, license coverage, a scan for file lookups next to a module, esbuild warnings, and an import in a directory with no `node_modules` | None in the esbuild config |

Both bundles use the same banner to define `require` with `createRequire`, because some bundled CommonJS dependencies call `require()`.

These differences could cause problems that might be difficult to find. For example, the two bundles could run different builds of the same package, or a fix in one config could be missing from the other.

### Proposal

We could have ai-lib build one self-contained headless bundle, as a second esbuild config next to the current one in `ai-provider-bridge/scripts/build-coordinator.ts`. The current config keeps all dependencies external. The new config could instead bundle them, with the output being a directory with the entry, its chunks, a `package.json`, and a notices file. Positron and Assistant could then copy this directory and not run esbuild on the entry themselves.

The checks I put together in posit-dev/positron#17276 could move to ai-lib with the bundle, and then each ai-lib change gets the checks (not only a Positron server build).

### Questions

1. Could ai-lib own this build output?
2. One file or lazy chunks? The chunks keep the AWS and Azure code from loading until a provider needs it, while one file is simpler to copy.
3. Which module resolution? Positron's current choice matches Node, so the bundle runs the same code as the unbundled packages. Assistant's choice is more like the esbuild default for many projects IIUC. Definitely I think one choice for both would be better than two.
4. Is one notices file next to the bundle enough for license compliance in both products?
5. Where do the output checks run? In ai-lib CI, in the consumers' builds, or maybe both?
